description:
The cursor (fz-sc8.208) made the interpreter slower wherever a binary is walked. Release `fz2 interp`, before the cursor (92cead0b2) against develop 9db393fac: a byte walk over 1.3 MB 17.86G -> 24.70G instructions; 2,000 JSON.decode calls 6.48G -> 8.32G; fixtures 01254 36.51G -> 41.94G and 01294 37.34G -> 44.48G, which puts them over the coverage job's 20 s CPU limit on interp (fz-9x7.10), so develop's push CI is red. Native run and build are unaffected.

Three causes, each confirmed by experiment on the cursor commit:
- `call_fixed_extern` (src/ir_interp/extern_call.rs) builds a Vec per parameter per call through `ExternTy::wire_classes(&[ty])`.
- `extern_argument_words` (src/ir_interp/backend.rs) builds the word Vec and one more Vec per input per call.
- `BoundValue::Transport` (src/compiler2/transport.rs) holds its lanes in a Vec, so a cursor, two words, is allocated, cloned and freed on every step.

With all three removed: byte walk 19.10G, JSON.decode 7.32G, 01254 37.60G, 01294 38.86G. A remainder of 3 to 13% is not located.

Done when: the three per-step allocations are gone; interp instructions on the byte-walk and JSON.decode probes are measured against develop built in the same environment; 01254 and 01294 pass the coverage step.
title: A walked binary passed in the interpreter allocates nothing per step
